query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

generation.hypothesis: The intervention of using machine learning-based prediction models, such as those utilizing high-throughput density-functional theory (DFT) calculations, can overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in their high-temperature solid and liquid states
generation.intervention: Machine learning-based prediction models using high-throughput DFT calculations
generation.conditions: High-temperature solid and liquid states, large compositional space
generation.structural_mediator: Single-phase solid solutions, body-centered cubic (BCC) structures
generation.mechanism: High melting point (Tm) as the primary driving factor for HEA formation, favorable mixing with high-melting elements
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved accuracy, availability, and efficiency in determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties
generation.boundary: Large compositional space of nearly ~ 10^8 types of HEAs, high-temperature solid and liquid states
generation.uncertainty: Limited availability of experimental data, complexity of high-entropy alloy systems

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of predicted and experimentally determined melting temperatures, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties for a set of multicomponent high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted values deviate significantly from the experimentally determined values, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How to systematically document experimentally reported high-entropy alloy microstructures and metallurgy-specific features to support machine learning-based phase classification?. System: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) comprising 1362 multicomponent alloys selected through the end of August 2020, excluding glassy, amorphous, and hexagonal close-packed phases. Processing: Synthesis routes, hot- or cold-working, homogenization (temperature and time), annealing (temperature and time), and quenching were extracted from peer-reviewed experimental articles. Test conditions: Data derived from experimental peer-reviewed research articles; no new experimental testing was performed in this data article. Findings: The dataset contains 1422 entries with seventeen columns covering identification, composition, empirical parameters, processing, and microstructure; The final dataset includes 1362 multicomponent alloys after removing entries with missing data and eliminating glas

Own digest: Paper card. Question: Which equimolar quinary combinations of 40 metallic elements form thermodynamically stable single-phase solid solutions, and what are the driving factors (mixing enthalpy, melting point, intermetallic competition) governing their formation?. System: Equimolar quinary alloys from 40 elements (e.g., AlCoMnNiV, CoFeMnNiZn, Cantor alloy CoCrFeMnNi). Processing: High-throughput density-functional theory (DFT) calculations using a binary regular solid-solution model; experimental synthesis via arc-melting (AlCoMnNiV) and mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering (CoFeMnNiZn). Test conditions: Thermodynamic stability assessed at temperatures ranging from 800 to 1600 K, with optimal screening at T = 0.9Tm; experimental validation via SEM, XRD, and EDS after heat treatment at 1373 K (AlCoMnNiV) and 1073–1273 K (CoFeMnNiZn).
